explanation: In Spain, beckoning someone with a curled index finger is considered rude and condescending, as it is typically used to call animals or children. This gesture is seen as disrespectful to adults, implying a lack of equality or dignity. A more polite approach is to use an open hand with the palm facing down and fingers together, moving them toward you.
local_tip: Instead, gesture with your whole hand, palm down, and wave your fingers toward you in a scooping motion.
regional_note: While this is consistent across most of Spain, in the Canary Islands the open-hand gesture is also preferred, but the finger beckon may be slightly less offensive among close friends.

also_check.note: Beckoning with the index finger is considered very rude and is used only for animals; use a palm-down wave instead.
This gesture is extremely offensive and can even lead to legal trouble; it is reserved for calling dogs.
While not as offensive as in Spain, it can be seen as overly familiar or dismissive; a polite verbal call is preferred.
